findings.title: Real-adapter pagination negatives no longer prove the error constructor required by the mapper
findings.rationale: api-app/src/integrations/meta/meta.client.spec.ts:169,181,186,191 now assert only rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'META_INDISPONIVEL' }); the previous constructor checks in these affected negative cases have been replaced. The new application boundary deliberately recognizes instanceof MetaIndisponivelError only (channels.service.ts:291). Its BFF/PG negative executes the separately implemented typed fake loop (flow:110-121; helpers.ts:72-84), while the browser uses another separately implemented typed fake (browser-server.cjs:3,94,97). Counterexample by source inspection, not an executed mutation: replacing a real pagination throw with Object.assign(new Error('safe inconclusive'), { code: 'META_INDISPONIVEL' }) preserves the newly asserted unit code and fetch counts. The independent typed-fake BFF/browser cases also remain satisfied, yet a real verify request bypasses instanceof and again returns generic 500. Class assertions elsewhere in this spec cover different operations and do not close that branch-specific hole. Why now: cp36d introduces constructor identity as the production transport-mapping predicate while replacing the exact adapter class assertions that could protect it. Current production throws are the correct class; this is a concrete regression-harness efficacy gap at the same error boundary just repaired, not a claim that current production already emits the wrong type. Blast radius is the persisted official-number unavailable/inconclusive response contract; no owner/DB security regression was found.
findings.suggested_action: A (recommended): for each affected invalid-grant/budget/cycle/oversized-cursor operation, retain its single rejected promise or captured rejection and assert both toBeInstanceOf(MetaIndisponivelError) and code META_INDISPONIVEL on that same result. Keep current scoped arguments and exact fetch-count assertions; do not call the operation a second time merely to inspect another property. This is a small test-only change with low implementation/runtime risk, one-spec blast radius, no added network/query cost and low maintenance. It restores the simple composition contract without altering the sound narrow production catch. Root should serialize it after the live review/run and refresh the affected evidence rather than attributing later bytes to this freeze. B: add a faithful real MetaHttpClient HTTP-stub -> service/BFF contract test for the same budget failure. That can prove the composition directly, but needs more wiring and maintenance than restoring the lost assertion. C: keep code-only units and rely on static inspection plus typed provider fakes. No immediate production edit is needed, but this leaves the concrete generic-500 regression undetected by the new harness; not recommended for closure of this repaired boundary. Broadening production mapping to any object with a matching code would change the approved error boundary and is not an appropriate test repair. Root owns the authoritative finding disposition, current validation and acceptance.
